proof_summary: Since \(2^{10n+2}\equiv4\pmod{66}\), the outer exponent is congruent to \(6\pmod{66}\), so Fermat-period reduction gives divisibility by \(67\). For every prime below \(67\), the proof similarly reduces the nested exponent using a short modular period (handling \(17\) separately) and checks the finitely many resulting residues, showing that none divides; hence \(67\) is the least prime factor.
